findings.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||, collapsing to effectively isTeamOwner and incorrectly denying plain team admins the intended permission

EventManager is constructed from ctx.user (the requester) rather than the booking organizer (booking.user), so calendar updates run with the wrong account's credentials when a non-organizer adds guests

Blacklist and duplicate-attendee email checks are case-sensitive against a lowercased blacklist and raw attendee emails, allowing a blacklisted or already-invited address to bypass the check via case variation

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the unfiltered 'guests' array instead of 'uniqueGuests', causing dropped duplicate/blacklisted guests that match an existing attendee to be misclassified as newly added and receive the wrong email template
guests array in addGuests.schema.ts has no upper bound on length, allowing unbounded attendee insertion/emailing as a spam/DoS vector
Any current attendee can add arbitrary new guests, leaking meeting details (location, video URL/password) to third parties without organizer consent
Email send failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are swallowed via console.log without preserving the actual error, hiding production notification failures

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed from ctx.user (the requester) rather than the booking organizer (booking.user), so calendar updates run with the wrong account's credentials when a non-organizer adds guests

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using an `EventManager` constructed from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. However, the booking organizer is separately loaded as `organizer` (and the booking includes `user` with `credentials`), and authorization allows non-organizers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner) to call this mutation. In those cases, the code will attempt to update the booking’s calendar event using the requester’s credentials rather than the organizer/booking owner’s credentials, which is a concrete correctness issue (likely failing to update the intended calendar or updating the wrong account).

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the unfiltered 'guests' array instead of 'uniqueGuests', causing dropped duplicate/blacklisted guests that match an existing attendee to be misclassified as newly added and receive the wrong email template

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already attendees and any `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, and only creates new attendees from `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original, unfiltered `guests` array. Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, classification is based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`: attendees whose email is in that array get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, otherwise they get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the input `guests` includes an email that was filtered out because it already existed (or was blacklisted but already present), that existing attendee will be misclassified as “new” and receive the scheduled template instead of the “guests added” notification. Passing `uniqueGuests` would align email classification with the actual added attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: guests array in addGuests.schema.ts has no upper bound on length, allowing unbounded attendee insertion/emailing as a spam/DoS vector

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` where `guests` is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)`/upper bound. The new `addGuestsHandler` then uses this array to (1) `createMany` attendee rows (`data: guestsFullDetails`) and (2) trigger calendar updates and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which ultimately builds `emailsToSend` and does `await Promise.all(...)` over all attendees. Because there is no size cap in the schema or handler, an authorized caller (organizer/attendee/team admin per the handler’s checks) can submit an arbitrarily large list and cause unbounded DB inserts and email sending/concurrency, which is a plausible spam/DoS vector introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any current attendee can add arbitrary new guests, leaking meeting details (location, video URL/password) to third parties without organizer consent

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly allows any current attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the request is permitted unless `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`. Once permitted, the handler updates booking attendees and constructs a `CalendarEvent` including `location` and `videoCallData` (meeting URL/password) and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`, which sends ICS/email updates to attendees/new guests. This means an existing attendee can add arbitrary third-party emails and cause meeting details to be sent/shared without organizer-only restriction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are swallowed via console.log without preserving the actual error, hiding production notification failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues, discarding the actual `err` and not propagating or otherwise reporting the failure. This will hide production notification failures and provides no actionable error detail. (The swallowing happens in the handler rather than inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, but the issue is present in the diff.)
